nodes.name: Electrochemical Ir loading on NiSe
nodes.procedure: By electrochemically loading highly dispersed Ir onto Ni-based precursors such as NiSe, we achieve the coupling of Ir loading and catalyst reconstruction, leading to the formation of an oxygen-dominant surface. The Ir content on PC-Ir/NiSe was determined to be ~0.6 wt % by inductively coupled plasma optical emission spectroscopy (ICP-OES, Table S1).
nodes.source_text: By electrochemically loading highly dispersed Ir onto Ni-based precursors such as NiSe... The Ir content on PC-Ir/NiSe was determined to be ~0.6 wt % by inductively coupled plasma optical emission spectroscopy

nodes.characterization_summary: PC-NiSe displays Bragg reflections matching Ni_{0.85}Se crystalline structure. With Ir loading, no significant peak shift nor metallic Ir peaks observed, indicating no Ir nanoparticle formation.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The X-ray diffraction (XRD) patterns (Figure 1b) of the as-prepared PC-NiSe display the same Bragg reflections in agreement with the Ni_{0.85}Se crystalline structure. With Ir loading, the XRD peaks did not show a significant shift nor metallic Ir peaks...

nodes.characterization_summary: PC-Ir/NiSe shows nanosheet structure after electrochemical loading of Ir.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Scanning electron microscope (SEM) images (Figure 1c and Figure S1) showed that the as-prepared PC-Ir/NiSe had a nanosheet structure after electrochemical loading of Ir.

nodes.characterization_summary: PC-Ir/NiSe shows high dispersion of Ir single atoms visible as bright spots in lattice scattering, confirmed by elemental mappings of Ir, Ni, O, and Se.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Aberration-corrected high-angle annular dark-field scanning transmission electron microscopy (AC-HAADF-STEM) clearly showed a high dispersion of Ir single atoms on NiSe, visible as bright spots in the lattice scattering (Figure 1d), which was further supported by atomic-level elemental mappings (Figure 1e).

nodes.characterization_summary: Ir content on PC-Ir/NiSe determined to be ~0.6 wt%.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Ir content on PC-Ir/NiSe was determined to be ~0.6 wt % by inductively coupled plasma optical emission spectroscopy (ICP-OES, Table S1).

nodes.characterization_summary: PC-NiSe: Se 3d at 54.9 eV (Se-Ni), Ni 2p Ni^0 at 852.5/870.5 eV, SeOx at 59.0 eV. PC-Ir/NiSe: increased O 1s M-OH/lattice oxygen, Se 3d nearly undetectable post-reconstruction.
nodes.evidence_snippet: XPS analysis of the Se 3d spectrum for PC-NiSe shows a peak at 54.9 eV... matching well with the Ni 2p XPS spectrum, where pronounced Ni^0 doublet peaks are observed at 852.5 and 870.5 eV... After electrochemical iridium loading, the O 1s spectrum reveals a significant increase in the intensity of M-OH species and lattice oxygen, while the Se 3d signal becomes nearly undetectable.

nodes.characterization_summary: Ir/NiOOH-Se@Cl shows higher proportion of γ-NiOOH active phase with I_{474/553} ratio increasing from 2.0 to 2.4 (1.47-1.57 V vs RHE) vs stable 1.3 for Ir/NiOOH-Se@OH.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The ratio of Raman peak area at 474 cm^{-1} to 553 cm^{-1} was used as an indicator... The results showed a significantly stronger 474 cm^{-1} peak in Ir/NiOOH-Se@Cl compared to that in Ir/NiOOH-Se@OH... with the I_{474/553} ratio increasing from 2.0 to 2.4...

nodes.characterization_summary: Ir/NiOOH-Se@Cl shows rapid lattice oxygen exchange: δ(Ni-^{18}O) at 454 cm^{-1} disappears in 15 s at 1.32 V vs RHE with emergence of δ(Ni-^{16}O) and ν(Ni-^{16}O) at 474 and 553 cm^{-1}. Ir/NiOOH-Se@OH shows slower exchange over 5 min.
nodes.evidence_snippet: At OCV, a Raman shift at 454 cm^{-1} attributable to δ(Ni-^{18}O) was observed... when the applied anodic voltage increased to 1.32 V vs RHE, the δ(Ni-^{18}O) vibration band disappeared in 15 s, and concurrently two new vibration peaks emerged at 474 cm^{-1} and 553 cm^{-1}...

nodes.characterization_summary: ^{18}O-labeled Ir/NiOOH-Se@Cl shows ^{34}O_2/^{32}O_2 ratio of 0.53 (LSV) and 0.57 (i-t test), higher than Ir/NiOOH-Se@OH (0.44 and 0.51), confirming greater LOM contribution.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The ^{34}O_2/^{32}O_2 ratio reached 0.53 (from LSV test) and 0.57 (from i-t test) over Ir/NiOOH-Se@Cl, significantly higher than that over Ir/NiOOH-Se@OH (0.44 from LSV test and 0.51 from i-t test)...

nodes.evidence_snippet: XPS analysis of Ir revealed that the binding energy of Ir in Ir/NiOOH-Se@Cl shifted by +0.48 eV compared to that in Ir/NiOOH-Se@OH... the Ni in Ir/NiOOH-Se@Cl after reaction displayed a nearly unchanged valence state as compared to that in the as-prepared Ir/NiOOH-Se@Cl.

nodes.characterization_summary: Ir/NiOOH-Se@Cl shows nearly twice the concentration of adsorbed OH^* compared to Ir/NiOOH-Se@OH at 1.4 V vs RHE.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Quasi in situ EPR measurements... demonstrated that Ir/NiOOH-Se@Cl had nearly twice the concentration of adsorbed OH^* compared to Ir/NiOOH-Se@OH at the same potential...

nodes.characterization_summary: PC-Ir/NiSe shows no visible particles or clusters, indicating high dispersion of Ir species.
nodes.evidence_snippet: High-resolution transmission electron microscopy (HRTEM) images of PC-Ir/NiSe did not show any visible particles or clusters (Figure S2), indicating a high dispersion of Ir species on NiSe.
